svg.title: A horizon changes which way the future goes
svg.desc: At four radii, future radial light cones tilt inward. The outward generator is vertical at the horizon and points toward smaller radius inside. The diagram uses regular ingoing coordinates, not singular Schwarzschild time. Cone slopes follow dr/dT = −1 and (r − rₛ)/(r + rₛ). T is a drawing coordinate, not a freely falling clock reading.

g.text: 29 / A HORIZON CHANGES WHICH WAY THE FUTURE GOES

svg.aria-label: Ingoing Eddington–Finkelstein time, drawn with T = v − r and c = 1.

svg.data-tex: \text{Inside: every future light direction goes to smaller }r.
svg.aria-label: Inside: every future light direction goes to smaller r.

g.text: Outside: an outward ray can escape.
